findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it an internet-routable endpoint. Although the attached security group only permits 3306 from the VPC CIDR today, the public exposure removes a key network boundary and any loosening of the ingress rule immediately exposes the database to the internet.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS storage volume and its snapshots, leaving database contents unencrypted at rest.

The MySQL 8.0 parameter group applied to the database does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the instance accepts unencrypted client connections; the PHP application connects with plain mysqli_connect, so credentials and query data traverse the network in cleartext.

The master password is supplied through var.password and stored in plaintext in Terraform state rather than being generated and held in Secrets Manager with rotation; the master username is the predictable 'admin' and IAM database authentication is not enabled.

The user_data script interpolates the RDS master username and var.password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user_data is readable from the instance metadata service by any process on the host or via an SSRF flaw in the hosted PHP app, leaking the database master credentials.

No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 (token-less metadata access) remains enabled. Combined with credentials embedded in user_data and a highly privileged instance profile, an SSRF in the PHP application would yield both the DB password and the role's temporary AWS credentials.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is declared, so the root volume that stores the plaintext DB credential file may be unencrypted at rest unless the account-level EBS default encryption is on.

The bootstrap installs httpd and serves the data-entry PHP page over plain HTTP with no TLS, and the instance's public DNS name is exported as an output, so submitted personal data and responses travel unencrypted.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the internet-facing web instance. Compromise of the web application yields near-total control of S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS, including privilege-escalation paths such as launching instances with other roles or modifying DB master passwords.

The database security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing unrestricted outbound traffic from the database tier and facilitating data exfiltration or C2 from a compromised host.

Port 3306 ingress is allowed from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only from the application server's security group, so any workload anywhere in the VPC can reach the database and attempt to authenticate as the admin master user.

The instance is launched into a subnet whose public DNS name is exported as an output and is guarded by aws_security_group.portal_sg (defined elsewhere), indicating direct internet reachability of a host holding master DB credentials and a wildcard IAM role; no private-subnet/load-balancer boundary is interposed.
